question: Network structure and consensus speed; nationwide manifesto vs p_g

metric_definitions.rho_obs_200_400: exp(slope of log e(t)), t ∈ [200, 400]; e = ‖x − 1c‖ on the giant component
metric_definitions.t_half_between: first round where the between-region TV dispersion ≤ ½ its start (None if not by the end of the run)
metric_definitions.conductance: cut(r, V∖r) / min(vol r, vol V∖r), per region
metric_definitions.theory_vs_obs: per world, decay rate 1 − ρ observed vs predicted: Spearman, mean log ratio, RMSE
metric_definitions.nationwide: win of the planner with a nationwide manifesto (top3; also ORACLE, uniform), p_g high − low

test_families.nationwide: high − low p_g, paired by seed, for top3/planner, oracle/planner and uniform/planner × (k̄ = 10, 20, 30, pooled): McNemar on wins and Wilcoxon on expected share, each Holm over its 12 tests

deviations: Spectra (λ₂, μ₂, ν₂) by SciPy on the CPU: at N = 10⁴ SciPy is ~5× faster than the GPU lobpcg path (provenance.spectra_gpu_vs_scipy; §1.1 'measured slower' exception).
'Standard strategies' are the X0 policy set via the batched runner; the observation-only players (BayesPlanner, Top-3 player) are X6's job and are not rerun here.
Heterogeneous long runs are 2000 rounds (the asymptotic tail is slow), homogeneous 400 (plan: ≥ 400).
